name: Kerbrute - Password Spray via Kerberos
description: Sprays one password against many domain users using Kerberos pre-authentication - faster than SMB spraying and does NOT generate Windows Event ID 4625 (failed logon), generating 4768 instead which is less commonly monitored. Ideal quiet spray option.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY KERBEROS SPRAY IS QUIETER THAN SMB SPRAY ===
SMB spray → Windows Event 4625 (An account failed to log on)
Kerberos spray → Windows Event 4768 (Kerberos AS-REQ) with error 0x18 (bad password)
4625 is universally watched by SIEMs. 4768 is less commonly alerted on.
Kerbrute uses the AS-REQ phase of Kerberos: it sends a pre-auth request for each
user/password combo - if the password is wrong, DC returns KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED.
No NTLM, no SMB connection, fewer artifacts.

=== CRITICAL: ACCOUNT LOCKOUT RISK ===
Passord spraying = account lockout is the #1 risk.
Before ANY spray, enumerate the lockout policy:
  crackmapexec smb <dc> -u user -p pass --pass-pol
  net accounts
Typical safe practice: 1 attempt per user, wait > lockout reset window between rounds.

=== KERBRUTE OUTPUT ===
Valid credential found:
  [+] VALID LOGIN: jsmith@INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL:Spring2022
Invalid:
  [-] Domain Account does not exist or domain cannot be contacted
Note: kerbrute userenum first to build a confirmed-valid user list before spraying.

=== WHICH TOOL WHEN ===
Kerbrute    → quiet, no 4625, requires user list, best for first spray
CME SMB     → fast, noisier (4625), also shows 'Pwn3d!' if local admin
DomainPasswordSpray → Windows-native, reads lockout policy automatically
rpcclient   → fallback when both SMB and Kerberos spray are blocked

=== SPRAY CANDIDATES ===
Good first passwords to try:
  - Current season + year (Spring2024, Winter2023)
  - Company name + number (Inlanefreight1!)
  - Welcome+year (Welcome2024!)
  - Password + number (Password1, Password123)
Build user list: ldapsearch, CME --users, or kerbrute userenum from OSINT names. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

defense.why_it_works: Kerbrute passwordspray sprays via Kerberos AS-REQs, which avoids generating 4625 failed-logon events (quieter than SMB/LDAP spraying).
defense.prerequisites: A domain user list, candidate password(s), and network access to the auth service.
defense.impact: Valid credentials found via a spray that leaves no 4625.
defense.detection: Failed-authentication bursts: Windows 4625 / Kerberos 4771; account lockouts (4740). Spraying = one password across MANY accounts (few failures each - a subtle, distributed pattern). Defender for Identity flags spraying.
defense.artifacts: 4768 AS-REQs across many accounts (not 4625); a Kerberos spray pattern.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768 (Result_Code=0x18 OR Pre_Authentication_Type=2)
| stats dc(Account_Name) as accts by Client_Address, bin(_time, 5m)
| where accts>10
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4768
| summarize accts=dcount(TargetUserName), fails=countif(Status == "0x18") by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where accts > 10
| sort by accts desc
// kerbrute spray shows as 4768 AS-REQ bursts (not 4625) across many accounts
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110.003 M1032 MFA] MFA defeats spraying; [M1027] strong/unique passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on distributed failed logons and impossible travel.
defense.evasion: Spray one password low-and-slow with delays to avoid lockouts and volume alerts; rotate source hosts; Kerberos-based spraying avoids 4625.
defense.misconfiguration: The domain's lockout policy is either disabled or set with a threshold high enough (e.g., 10 attempts before lockout) that a low-and-slow spray - one guess per account per 30 minutes - never triggers lockout. Additionally, many accounts share the same simple passwords (company name + year, Season+Year), and the bad-password counter resets after the observation window elapses.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak lockout policy (domain default or intentionally lenient):
# Fine-Grained Password Policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# LockoutObservationWindow: 00:30:00
# LockoutThreshold:         0          <-- DISABLED! No lockout ever
# OR: LockoutThreshold: 10 (attacker sprays 9 per window, never locks)

# Also: accounts with password = company name:
# Common passwords: Summer2023!, Winter2024!, CompanyName1!
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong lockout policy:
# Via Default Domain Policy or Fine-Grained Password Policy (PSO):
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5
# LockoutThreshold 5 means 5 bad attempts in 30 min = 30-min lockout

# Fine-Grained PSO for admins (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name AdminPSO \
    -LockoutThreshold 3 -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 01:00:00 \
    -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject AdminPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Enable Azure AD / Entra ID Password Protection (bans common passwords):
# Also available on-premises via the Azure AD Password Protection agent

# Monitor Event 4740 (Account Locked Out) - spray leaves a cluster of these

explain:
Sprays a password over Kerberos - faster and quieter than SMB spraying:
  kerbrute passwordspray   one AS-REQ per user (no SMB logon events)
  -d <domain>              the domain
  --dc <dc_ip>             the Domain Controller
  <userlist>               usernames to try
  <password>               the single password sprayed
Generates Event 4768 (less monitored) instead of 4625. Stay under the lockout threshold per observation window; validate a hit with crackmapexec.
